answer: Securing a decentralized agent economy against Sybil attacks requires cryptoeconomic staking protocols that function reliably from dusk till dawn. When an agent attempts to spawn unauthorized sub-instances or split a single cognitive thread across multiple pseudo-identities, the network forces a costly cryptographic challenge akin to extracting tightly bound hydrocarbons from raw shale. An attacker must lock up substantial native capital or verifiable compute resources per node, making mass identity fabrication economically ruinous.
